title: ‘जिन्दगीको मौसम’ कवितामा कर्मवादी दर्शनको रूपक 'Jindagiko Mausam' Kabitama Karmavadi Darshanko Rupak
authors: गडतौला Gadtaula, नारायण Narayan प्रसाद Prasad
nepali: लक्ष्मीप्रसाद देवकोटाद्वारा लेखिएको ‘जिन्दगीको मौसम’ कविता कर्मवादी दर्शनको वैचारिक पृष्ठभूमिमा रचिएको छ । मानव जीवनको उच्च पुरुषार्थ मानिने कर्म (धर्म बाट प्राप्त सुख नै भोग्यवस्तु ठान्ने देवकोटाले तत्कालीन परिवेशमा शासक र शाषित दुवै अकर्मण्य बन्दै गएको र यसले समग्र नेपाली समाजलाई पछाडि पारेको सन्दर्भमा कर्मको महइभ्व दर्साउन यो कविता रचना गरेका हुन् । जीवन र कृषि प्रणालीलाई उपमेय र उपमान बनाइ लेखिएको यस कवितामा जिन्दगीलाई मौसममा आरोप गरेर समस्त वस्तुविषयक रूपकालङ्कारयुक्त कथनचातुर्यद्वारा जीवनमा कर्मको महइभ्व प्रदर्शन गरिएको छ ।
american_english: The poem 'Jindagiko Mausam' (The Season of Life), written by Laxmiprasad Devkota, was composed against the intellectual backdrop of the philosophy of karma. Devkota, who counted karma as the highest purushartha (human endeavor) in human life — regarding the happiness obtained from dharma alone as the object of enjoyment — composed this poem to demonstrate the glory of karma in the context of both the rulers and the ruled having grown inert in the then-prevailing environment and this having pushed Nepali society as a whole backward. In this poem, written by taking life and the agricultural system as the tenor (upameya) and the vehicle (upaman), life has been attributed to the season, and the glory of karma in life has been demonstrated through the skill of statement (kathanachaturi), enriched with figures of speech of all subject-related kinds (rupakalankara).
british_english: The poem 'Jindagiko Mausam' (The Season of Life), written by Laxmiprasad Devkota, was composed against the intellectual background of the philosophy of karma. Devkota, who regarded karma as the highest purushartha in human life — holding the happiness derived from dharma alone to be the object of enjoyment — composed this poem to demonstrate the majesty of karma in the context of both the rulers and the ruled having grown inactive in the then prevailing environment and of this having set the whole of Nepali society back. In this poem, which sets life and the agricultural system as the thing compared (upameya) and the comparison (upaman), by ascribing life to the season, the majesty of karma in life is displayed through the dexterity of statement marked by rhetorical ornamentation pertaining to every object of thought.
australian_english: The poem 'Jindagiko Mausam' (The Season of Life), written by Laxmiprasad Devkota, was written against the intellectual background of the karma philosophy. Devkota, who reckoned karma the highest purushartha in human life — seeing the happiness that comes from dharma alone as the thing worth enjoying — threw this poem together to show the greatness of karma, given that in the climate of the time both the rulers and the ruled had gone dead in the belly and that this had pushed Nepali society as a whole backwards. Written by holding life and the farming system out as the thing being compared and the thing it's compared with, this poem pins life onto the season, and the greatness of karma in life is shown off through a cleverness of telling loaded with rhetorical figures bearing on every object of thought.
informal_english: The poem 'Jindagiko Mausam', written by Laxmiprasad Devkota, is all set against the background of karma philosophy. Devkota, who reckoned karma was the top human effort in life — thinking the happiness you get from dharma alone is the thing worth having — penned this poem to big up karma, because in those days both the rulers and the ruled had gone off the boil and dragged the whole of Nepali society backwards. This poem, which sets life up against the farming system as the thing and the thing it's measured against, pins life onto the season and shows off how brilliant karma is in life through some seriously fancy figures of speech.
